subject: Biotechnology
title: The Future of Farm Biotech
description: A 60-second lesson on The Future of Farm Biotech.

hook.text: Farms that grow themselves — self-fertilizing crops, autonomous greenhouses, and AI-designed seeds.

buildup.text: Engineering cereal crops to fix their own nitrogen could eliminate synthetic fertilizer dependency worldwide.

discovery.text: De-extinction projects aim to revive lost crop ancestors — unlocking wild genetics erased by centuries of breeding.

twist.text: Farmers in developing nations often lack access to biotech advances — equity gaps could widen global food inequality.

climax.text: Open-source seed initiatives share engineered traits freely — democratizing access to climate-ready crops.

punchline.text: Smarter seeds, greener farms — agricultural biotech feeds the future.

quiz.question: Why could engineering nitrogen fixation into cereals be transformative?
options: It would make crops grow twice as fast
It could eliminate the need for synthetic fertilizers, reducing costs and environmental damage
It would make crops resistant to all known diseases
